correctness.rationale: For a guaranteed p-cycle with p prime and fully known p×p binary signature b_i(t)=1_{f^t(x_i)<=x_i}, label the phase a_j by f^{a_j}(x_1)=x_j. The time-zero-cleared row of x_{i+1} equals A_i(t+a_{i+1}), where A_i is the length-p indicator of the already known phase set S_i. A nonempty proper subset of additive Z/p has no nonzero translational stabilizer. Thus one cyclic rotation is unique and linear-time KMP matching in the doubled word recovers each of p-1 phases in O(p) steps and O(p) auxiliary storage. The reconstructed permutation maps phase a_i to a_i+1. Independently exhaustive enumeration checks all 1, 2, 24, 720 p-cycles for p=2,3,5,7, with an independent rotation matcher; tests corroborate and group-action proof covers all primes. Complexity applies to explicit full signatures, not unknown-signature or bit-precise input lower bounds.
